question: What is a measured single-target rho reference on Q1477's exact public N53 point under one worker and no cross-target table?

rho_method.partition_rule: low four native normal-basis x-coordinate bits of the current group point
rho_method.transition: R <- R + alpha_i G + beta_i Q; update both known coefficients modulo r
rho_method.distinguished_rule: low ten native normal-basis x-coordinate bits are zero
rho_method.walk_start: fresh deterministic nonzero coefficients a,b, starting at aG+bQ
rho_method.collision_recovery: for equal distinguished points, solve (a_old-a_new)/(b_new-b_old) modulo prime r and independently replay kG=Q
rho_method.stop_rule: verified scalar, 50000000 walk steps, or 1800 seconds of native online time

measurement.online_start: immediately before target-dependent validation and partition-point construction; process launch and point decoding are outside
measurement.online_stop: after recovered scalar replays to the same public target, or declared cap
measurement.operation_counts: all field mul/sqr/inv, point additions/doublings, walk steps, failed walks, distinguished-point records, and collision checks
measurement.memory: peak child RSS and distinguished-point table size
measurement.comparison_limit: Q1477's target subgroup check was before its query-through-replay clock, so do not report a controlled primary speedup ratio

controls: pre-run known-scalar toy collision tests on small exact curves
source-bound point arithmetic inherited from Q1468 and exact N53 field data
independent checked-Sage replay of the collision equation, recovered scalar, same Q1477 public point, and workload binding
claim_scope: paired N53 single-target rho reference only; no N83 compact solver, N131 complete work, or speedup promotion
